title: 2009 AMC 8 Problem 18
statement: The diagram represents a \(7\)-foot-by-\(7\)-foot floor that is tiled with \(1\)-square-foot shaded tiles and unshaded tiles. Notice that the corners have unshaded tiles. If a \(15\)-foot-by-\(15\)-foot floor is to be tiled in the same manner, how many unshaded tiles will be needed?

solutions.text:
In the \(7\times7\) example, there are \(4\) rows that contain \(4\) unshaded tiles, for \(4^2=16\) unshaded tiles.

For a \(15\times15\) floor with the same pattern, there will be \(8\) such rows with \(8\) unshaded tiles each.

Thus the number of unshaded tiles is \(8^2=64.\)

Thus, C is the correct answer.
hints: Look for the pattern in the unshaded tiles of the \(7\times7\) floor.
For an odd side length \(2k-1,\) the unshaded tile count follows \(k^2.\)
